info.name: VMS Backend - Visitor Management System
info.description:
Complete API for the Visitor Management System.

THREE CALLER TYPES, three different credentials:
  1. Staff (admin website) -> Authorization: Bearer <JWT>
  2. Visitor (their phone) -> invite token in the URL, no login
  3. Kiosk tablet          -> X-Device-Token header

GETTING STARTED:
  1. Run 'Auth > Login (Global Admin)' - it auto-saves the token
  2. Run 'Kiosk > Pair device' with code 123456 - auto-saves device token
  3. Everything else will then work.

Seeded logins:
  abhinav@company.com / Admin@12345   (Global Admin, all 43 permissions)
  priya@company.com   / Security@123  (Security Desk)
  suresh@company.com  / Host@12345    (Host - own visitors only)
  meera@company.com   / Approve@123   (Approvals Admin)

request.description: VIP skips the approval queue entirely.
One action, SEPARATE token per person. Bad rows fail individually.
Generates a NEW token - the old link stops working.
What the visitor sees. private_notes are NEVER returned here.
In dev mode the response includes dev_code so you can test without Twilio.
Must happen BEFORE face capture. Set accepted=false to test the opt-out path.
Raw base64 or a data URL. Blocked if consent was not given.
One-time code. Saves device_token automatically. Code cannot be reused.
Returns only name and department - no emails, no roles.
The one endpoint the tablet uses for everything. Returns suggested_action so the kiosk never has to ask 'are you going out or coming in?'
Visit stays OPEN, pass stays valid, host is deliberately NOT notified.
No form, no OTP, no approval. Flags confirm_still_visiting if away over 2 hours.
Different action from step-out. This closes the visit for good.
The kiosk polls this. Countdown, and a NEUTRAL message if denied.
A host without approval permissions only sees their own queue.
Gated behind its own permission - it exposes blocklist reasons.
The reason is internal. The visitor only sees 'Please speak to reception'.
Every visit, and every entry/step-out/step-in/exit inside each one.
Removes biometric data without touching visit history.
Someone forgot to scan out. Recorded as manual, not a fake face scan.
Creates a NEW row. The original is never overwritten.
Deactivates, never hard-deletes - their past visits must stay intact.
Shows '(You)' next to the logged-in user.
Two-step New admin modal. Emails an 'Accept invite' link.
Also logs that person out everywhere. You cannot remove your own access.
All 43 permissions grouped by module and sub-category. The Roles screen renders its checkboxes from this.
System roles cannot be deleted.
online = seen in the last 5 minutes. needs_attention drives the orange nav dot.
Instantly kills that tablet's access.
The one number worth tuning with real faces before your demo.
Match rate, average score, how often the OTP fallback was needed.
Append-only. There is deliberately no PATCH or DELETE endpoint here.
Expire invites, auto-close stale visits, escalate approvals, purge old face data.
Log in as suresh@company.com first, then run this. Proves permissions are enforced on the backend, not just hidden in the UI.
A kiosk token can NEVER reach an admin endpoint.
And an admin token cannot act as a kiosk either.
